info.name: Rental Car Booking API - Presentation Demo
info.description:
Rental Car Booking API, 7-minute presentation demo. Self-contained, re-runnable, no server-side helper scripts.
Run it in Postman (Collection Runner, run order as listed, import demo.postman_environment.json and set baseUrl, adminEmail, adminPassword) or with: npm run demo.
Start the API normally (npm start, NODE_ENV=development) so the login limiter is ON. With NODE_ENV=test the limiter is off and the single 429 assertion is reported as skipped.

Run-time data: the collection pre-request script creates a random runId on the first request and derives every email, promo code and date from it and from today's UTC date. Nothing is shared between runs, so the demo can run on a dirty database.

LOGIN BUDGET (the limiter allows 10 POST /auth/login per minute per IP, counted whether the login succeeds or not; register does not count):
 #1 2.3 login A, #2 2.7 login A again, #3 3.1 admin login  = 3
 #4..#8 9.2-9.6 five wrong passwords on the throwaway user  = 5 (the 5th locks the account)
 #9 9.7 correct password on the locked account              = 1  -> 9 logins, one below the limit
 #10 9.8 flood iteration 1: unknown email, still allowed (401)
 #11 9.8 flood iteration 2: the limiter answers 429.
The 429 demonstration is last and the lockout demonstration is before it. Run the demo at most once per minute per machine (wait 60 s between runs), otherwise the previous run's logins still count. Everything before the flood stays at 9 logins, so a fresh minute is all it needs.
The 20-way atomic promo race is shown from the terminal: node scripts/promo-race.js (see README).

exec: // Runs before every request. A new run (first request) generates fresh run-time data.
const FIRST = '1.1 List providers (public, no token)';
const day = (n) => { const d = new Date(); d.setUTCHours(0, 0, 0, 0); return new Date(d.getTime() + n * 86400000).toISOString().slice(0, 10); };
// future bookings of user A (the 4th is refused), the booking edit, the promo validity and the stats range
set('a1Date', day(10)); set('a1Ret', day(12)); set('a1NewRet', day(13));
// late return: returnDate = today (UTC) minus 2 days; the actual return is 3 h after that day's 23:59:59.999Z anchor (yesterday 02:59:59.999Z, in the past, inside the 24 h future bound)
pm.test('both seeded providers are listed (Alpha Rentals, Beta Cars)', function () { pm.expect(find('Alpha Rentals')).to.be.an('object'); pm.expect(find('Beta Cars')).to.be.an('object'); });
const a = find('Alpha Rentals'), b = find('Beta Cars');
pm.collectionVariables.set('betaId', b._id); pm.collectionVariables.set('betaRate', String(b.dailyRate)); pm.collectionVariables.set('betaLate', String(b.lateFeePerHour));
console.log('Alpha Rentals dailyRate=' + a.dailyRate + ', Beta Cars dailyRate=' + b.dailyRate + ' lateFeePerHour=' + b.lateFeePerHour);
pm.test('it is Alpha Rentals', function () { pm.expect(pm.response.json().data.name).to.eql('Alpha Rentals'); });
pm.test('response has a token and the user, and no password', function () {
pm.test('duplicate email -> 400 Email already registered', function () { pm.response.to.have.status(400); pm.expect(pm.response.json().message).to.eql('Email already registered'); });
pm.test('me is user A with role user', function () { const d = pm.response.json().data; pm.expect(d.email).to.eql(pm.collectionVariables.get('emailA')); pm.expect(d.role).to.eql('user'); });

item.name: 2.5 Logout (revokes the token on the server)

exec: pm.test('revoked token is refused -> 401', function () { pm.response.to.have.status(401); });

item.name: 2.7 Login user A again for the working session (login #2)

exec: pm.test('a new token, different from the revoked one', function () { pm.expect(t).to.be.a('string'); pm.expect(t).to.not.eql(pm.collectionVariables.get('tokenA1')); });
pm.test('admin token and role admin', function () { const j = pm.response.json(); pm.expect(j.token).to.be.a('string'); pm.expect(j.data.role).to.eql('admin'); });

item.name: 3.3 User A books Alpha Rentals (2 days)

exec: pm.test('totalPrice = dailyRate x 2 days = ' + expected, function () { pm.expect(d.totalPrice).to.eql(expected); });
console.log('booking 1: totalPrice ' + d.totalPrice + ' (dailyRate ' + pm.collectionVariables.get('alphaRate') + ' x 2 days)');

item.name: 3.6 User A tries a 4th booking (limit is 3)

exec: pm.test('4th booking -> 400 (at most 3 cars)', function () { pm.response.to.have.status(400); pm.expect(pm.response.json().message).to.include('at most 3'); });

item.name: 3.7 User B reads user A booking

exec: pm.test('another user cannot read it -> 403', function () { pm.response.to.have.status(403); });

item.name: 3.9 User B books Beta Cars with a pickup 3 days ago (for the late-return demo)

exec: pm.test('totalPrice = Beta dailyRate x 1 day', function () { pm.expect(d.totalPrice).to.eql(Number(pm.collectionVariables.get('betaRate'))); });

item.name: 4.1 Admin creates a promo (10 percent, maxRedemptions 1)

exec: pm.test('code stored upper-case with maxRedemptions 1', function () { pm.expect(d.code).to.eql(pm.collectionVariables.get('promoCode')); pm.expect(d.maxRedemptions).to.eql(1); });
pm.test('the new code is listed', function () { pm.expect(pm.response.json().data.map((p) => p.code)).to.include(pm.collectionVariables.get('promoCode')); });

item.name: 4.3 User A applies the code to their booking

exec: pm.test('discount applied: 10 percent of ' + before, function () { pm.expect(d.discount).to.eql(before * 0.1); });
pm.test('totalPrice reduced to ' + before * 0.9, function () { pm.expect(d.totalPrice).to.eql(before * 0.9); pm.expect(d.totalPrice).to.be.below(before); });

item.name: 4.4 User B applies the SAME code (sequential redemption limit)

exec: pm.test('second redemption -> 400 maximum redemptions', function () { pm.response.to.have.status(400); pm.expect(pm.response.json().message).to.eql('Promo code has reached its maximum redemptions'); });
// The 20-way concurrent race is proven from the terminal: node scripts/promo-race.js

5.2 Admin edits the return date of user A booking
